item.base_system: Equimolar powder mixture of Cu, Mo, Ta, W, and V
item.intervention: Partial sintering using spark plasma sintering (SPS) to create a consolidated target
item.processing: Vacuum atmosphere, 1000 °C, heating rate 100 °C/min to 800 °C then 50 °C/min to 1000 °C, soaking 5 min, pressure 40 MPa up to 900 °C then decreased to 20 MPa
item.structure_change: Formation of a single target with uniform distribution of all elemental phases
quotes: A sputtering target was developed by partial sintering of an equimolar powder mixture of Cu, Mo, Ta, W, and V using spark plasma sintering.
The elemental maps from the cross section of the target in Figure 1 b showed a uniform distribution of all of the elemental phases.
A single target containing the principal elements, CuMoTaWV, was partially sintered at 1000 °C using SPS to lower the cost and time of target preparation

item.intervention: DC-magnetron sputtering deposition on Si and 304 stainless-steel substrates
item.processing: Argon atmosphere, 500 °C substrate temperature, 8 rpm rotation, 150 W power, 120 min duration
item.structure_change: Formation of a nanocrystalline RHEA film with thickness ~900 nm, average grain size 18 nm, and body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution with (110) preferred orientation
item.property_change: Hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa
item.attributed_mechanism: Nanocrystalline nature resulting in grain boundary strengthening
quotes: The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film with a thickness of ∼900 nm and an average grain size of 18 nm.
X-ray diffraction of the film revealed a body-centered cubic solid solution with preferred orientation in the (110) directional plane.
The nanocrystalline nature of the RHEA film resulted in a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: CuMoTaWV equimolar target. Intervention: DC-magnetron sputtering deposition on Si and 304 stainless-steel substrates. Property change: Hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa. Mechanism: Nanocrystalline nature resulting in grain boundary strengthening. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film with a thickness of ∼900 nm and an average grain size of 18 nm."

item.intervention: Fabrication of 440-nm-diameter nanopillars for compression testing
item.processing: Focused ion beam (FIB) milling with high current (1 nA) followed by low current (320 pA) polishing
item.test_conditions: Microcompression using Anton Paar ultra-nanoindentation tester, max force 3 mN, loading rate 1 mN/min
item.structure_change: Intergranular fracture behavior along textured columnar grains
item.property_change: Compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa (yield strength 10.7 ± 0.8 GPa)
item.attributed_mechanism: Combined effect of solid solution hardening, grain size, and grain boundary strengthening
quotes: A focused ion beam (FIB) was used to create four nanopillars for compression tests.
A high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa was obtained in nanopillar compression due to solid solution hardening and grain boundary strengthening.

The extremely high compressional strength of the BCC HEA nanopillar has been attributed to the combined effect of a substantial solid solution hardening effect, grain size, and grain boundary strengthening.

item.intervention: Annealing at 300 °C with a heating rate of 2 °C/min in argon atmosphere
item.processing: Annealing at 300 °C, 2 °C/min heating rate, argon atmosphere
item.structure_change: Lowest surface roughness (Sa 2 nm, Sq 3 nm) and improved grain morphology compared to higher temperatures
item.property_change: Increased adhesion between the RHEA film and 304 stainless-steel substrates
item.attributed_mechanism: Annealing improved adhesion and surface roughness
quotes: The adhesion between the RHEA film and 304 stainless-steel substrates was increased on annealing.
The annealed CuMoTaWV film at 300 °C ( Figure 10 a) showed the lowest surface roughnesses of 2 nm (Sa) and 3 nm (Sq).
Annealing the CuMoTaWV RHEA film at 300 °C improved the surface roughness through grain refinement and increased the adhesion of the film to the steel substrate

item.intervention: Wear test against E52100 alloy steel counterball at room temperature (RT)
item.processing: Ball-on-disc setup, 1 N load, 0.1 m/s sliding speed
item.structure_change: Excessive plastic deformation and smearing of the film due to low film adhesion
item.property_change: Average coefficient of friction (COF) of 0.2 up to 15 m, then increasing to 0.7; wear rate 6.4 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/N m
item.attributed_mechanism: Low film adhesion leading to film removal
quotes: For the wear test against the E52100 alloy steel (Grade 25, 700–880 HV) at 1 N load, the RHEA film showed an average coefficient of friction (COF) and wear rate of 0.25 (RT) and 1.5 (300 °C), and 6.4 × 10 –6 mm 3 /N m (RT) and 2.5 × 10 –5 mm 3 /N m (300 °C), respectively.

The wear test of the as-deposited RHEA film showed an average coefficient of friction (COF) of 0.2 up to a sliding distance of 15 m, after which the COF increased to 0.7, suggesting the removal of the film from the substrate.
The wear test of the as-deposited RHEA film showed excessive plastic deformation and smearing of the film due to low film adhesion, as shown in Figure 12 a, resulting in an increase in COF.

quotes: In contrast, the wear behavior of the annealed high-entropy film showed an average COF of 0.25 up to a 30 m sliding distance, followed by a slight increase to 0.3, and remained the same until the end of the test, suggesting an improvement in the film response to wear and its adhesion to the substrate on annealing.
